blocks.c: Here is where I nearly lost it.

Because it was right. That is the thing about the whole affair that I have never got clear of. Every threat that building ever made me was accurate, and every rule it followed it followed exactly, and if I had walked away at any point in eleven days it would have let me, and a man would have started work at nine and taken the freight car and never come back and nobody would have known.
It is not a monster. It is worse. It is a correctly functioning system that nobody has read.
"I dispute the characterisation of occupation," I said.

"Noted. Disputes are held pending determination, and there is no time to determine them before renewal, so the dispute will be held and the renewal will proceed, and the dispute will then be determined by default, because the material time will have passed." It sounded almost sympathetic. "Clause fourteen is a very good clause, Mr. Oduya. Ms. Aguilar has used it beautifully for thirty-one years. But it is a delaying clause. It has never been anything else. You cannot win with it; you can only be slow with it."
"I know," I said. "I'm not using clause fourteen."
I put both log books on the counter.
"I'm using page ten," I said, "and I'd like you to define, for the record, in front of a witness, what the current maintenance log of these premises is."
For the first time, the shape behind the counter stopped moving entirely.
Then it said, and its voice had gone flat and careful in a way that made every hair on my arms stand up:
"Then which one is it?" I said. "Because we've both been writing in ours this morning."
